notes.text: Close gradually around the bottle neck while holding the initial pose; check tactile contact before lifting.
Light neck contact is visible. Secure the opening and begin a slow vertical lift, watching for bottle retention.
The bottle neck rises with the fingers. Continue lifting slowly with a slight motion toward the wall, keeping its base nearby.
Continue the supported lift; the neck is retained and the bottle is beginning to tip upright beside the wall.
Lift the neck another small increment while following its arc toward the wall; maintain the light pinch.
The bottle remains held and its base stays by the wall. Continue raising and moving the neck inward to bring it toward upright.
Follow the bottle's supported pivot: slightly more motion toward the wall and less vertical rise as it approaches upright.
Continue drawing the held neck above the nearby base, reducing lift as the bottle becomes steeper.
Bring the neck closer above the base with a gentle inward arc, keeping the bottle supported near the wall.
The bottle is nearly upright. Bring the neck a little farther over its base without appreciably raising the base.
Make a small final alignment toward vertical and settle the base on the support, retaining the neck until its posture is checked.
The bottle appears upright with its base on the table beside the wall. Gently open the fingers without moving the arm to release it.

Raise the retained neck along a gradual arc toward upright; monitor the base against the support and wall.
Continue lifting and bring the neck closer over the base, with the bottle still securely pinched.
Reduce vertical speed while bringing the neck toward the wall, continuing to pivot the bottle toward upright.
Approach upright more gently, shifting the neck over the base with only a small additional rise.
Bring the neck nearly above the base while keeping its height steady and avoiding the wall.
Tilt the wrist away from the wall with translation compensation to preserve the neck location and create clearance for upright placement.
Align the neck more closely over the base and lower slightly toward support contact before releasing.

Continue the slow upward pivot, increasing motion toward the bottle base as the bottle becomes steeper. Keep the established neck opening.
Follow the bottle neck upward and toward its planted base, with decreasing vertical increments as it approaches upright.
The bottle is still inclined with the base on the surface. Raise and bring the neck closer over that base while retaining the grasp.
Bring the neck farther over the near-wall base with a smaller upward increment; the bottle is approaching vertical but not yet upright.
Angle the hand away from the wall about the retained neck, compensating position so the bottle stays near its support while gaining wrist clearance.

The bottle is nearly upright. Make a small final neck-centering motion toward its base with only a slight rise, keeping the base beside the wall.
Settle the nearly vertical bottle onto the surface with a short gentle descent, then gradually release while holding the hand still.
Contact has cleared and the bottle is on the surface. Withdraw the open fingers upward and away from the wall, then check that it stands independently.

notes.text: Maintain the native grasp and turn gently about the vertical key axis; monitor tactile deformation for resistance.
Continue turning in place while keeping the key seated and the grasp unchanged; tactile contact remains broadly round.
Keep turning about the slot axis in small increments; no clear resistance deformation yet.
Continue a controlled positive turn without lateral or vertical motion, watching for a change in tactile contact.
Tactile contact remains stable; continue turning gently in place toward the mechanical stop.
Continue the slow axial turn with position and grasp held fixed; watch both tactile views for resistance.
Keep the key centered and seated while continuing the positive turn; tactile contact has not shown a clear stop yet.
Continue with finer angular steps to detect the first tactile sign of mechanical resistance without shifting the key.
Maintain the seated key and continue the fine positive turn; tactile views still show no clear torsional stop.
Continue small axial rotation increments, holding the grasp and insertion depth while watching for tactile shear at the stop.
The tactile contact is still rounded without a clear stop. Continue the controlled positive turn at fixed insertion depth.
Keep the grasp closed and rotate in place, checking for the tactile deformation that indicates mechanical resistance.
Both tactile views now show torsional deformation consistent with the stop. Ease back slightly to unload twist before a straight extraction.
Torsional deformation has relaxed. Hold the attained angle and begin a slow, straight upward extraction without lateral motion.
The tactile patches shifted during the lift, suggesting axial resistance. Remove that small lift and ease the twist slightly before retrying straight extraction.
Test a small straight pull at the relaxed angle; compare tactile patch motion to distinguish release from continued axial loading.
The pull still loads the tactile patches. Reseat and approach the positive stop again with finer rotation rather than increasing extraction force.
A flat edge in the left tactile patch indicates renewed rotational resistance. Hold this angle and test a small straight upward pull.
The small pull still shifts the contacts rather than clearly freeing the key. Reseat, then advance the turn slightly to locate the stop more precisely.
Opposed flat tactile edges confirm torsional loading. Unwind a little farther to remove stored twist while keeping the key seated and firmly held.
The tactile contacts have returned to their unloaded shape. Retry a slow, straight upward pull at this relaxed angle and check whether the key follows.
Pause at the small extraction offset to distinguish transient tactile lag from sustained axial resistance, keeping orientation and grasp unchanged.
The contact shift eased while holding. Continue a short, slow straight pull and inspect whether deformation grows or the key follows upward.
Maintain the relaxed angle and continue a slow axial extraction. Contact remains present; monitor the exposed key and any increasing slip.
The key appears to follow upward and tactile displacement is not accumulating sharply. Continue straight extraction at the same slow speed.
Continue pulling vertically with the angle fixed and grasp unchanged; tactile contact remains steady as more of the key emerges.

Unload and bring yaw back near the socket's visible axis while shifting depth slightly away from the camera. Compensate lateral tip motion during the rotation.
Reapproach vertically at the refined depth and near-neutral yaw. Check whether the plug advances without sliding along the fingers.
Use a fine depth sweep away from the camera at shallow mouth contact, with minimal descent, to locate the narrow opening without further axial slip.
The depth sweep tilted the plug against a constrained tip. Reverse that lateral load toward the camera while slightly relieving contact, then reassess centering.
Unload the tip, center depth between the two opposite contact tilts, and refine yaw using the opposed tactile offsets while preserving tip centering.
Close the small gap with a submillimeter lateral recentering and slow vertical approach at the selected depth and yaw.
The tip has reached the mouth with stable tactile contact. Test another slow millimeter of insertion without changing alignment.
Unload the rim and correct yaw in the opposite direction indicated by the paired tactile offsets, with a small pitch refinement and approximate tip-pivot compensation.
Reapproach the mouth with the refined pitch and opposite yaw correction; retain the grip and monitor contact stability.
Test shallow insertion at the current alignment with a quarter-millimeter depth refinement; use tactile stability to distinguish seating from slip.
The tactile edges flatten under rim contact, indicating a depth-induced bend. Relieve slightly and shift toward the camera to restore the unloaded plug angle.
The contact slope has returned near its unloaded value. Test a slow insertion with a very small rightward centering adjustment.
Relieve the rim and remove a small residual forward pitch while approximately preserving the tip position. The present yaw appears consistent with the tactile offsets.
Test slow axial insertion with the refined pitch and yaw, keeping depth and lateral centering fixed while checking tactile displacement.
Relieve the shallow contact and shift depth slightly toward the camera to remove the tactile-indicated bend, then gently re-test the opening.
Continue the fine depth correction with only a half-millimeter axial advance, seeking the unloaded tactile angle at the socket mouth.
Depth-induced pitch is now nearly relieved, but opposed tactile offsets suggest residual yaw. Lift clear and rotate farther toward positive yaw with tip-centering compensation.
Reapproach the slot with the larger positive-yaw correction, preserving depth and grip while checking whether the tip advances without sliding.
Contact is stable after the approach. Test a gentle one-millimeter insertion at the current yaw, watching for plug advance versus axial slip.
The larger yaw still slips at the rim. Return to the smaller yaw, unload the tip, and modestly reduce gripper opening to retain the connector during a fresh approach.
Test a slow straight insertion with the reduced opening target, checking whether the connector advances rather than sliding.
The current tactile slope indicates residual forward lean. Correct that pitch by a small tip-centered pivot while relieving contact, rather than pressing farther.
The pitch pivot preserved the tactile contact while bringing the plug closer to upright. Test a slow straight insertion without further angular changes.
Axial slip persists despite the pitch correction. Relieve contact and test a one-millimeter lateral correction, which may be hidden by the coarse head-image alignment.
Lift the retained connector fully clear of the socket to remove accumulated slip and contact-induced tilt before measuring a fresh alignment.
Hold clear of the socket and restore the original opening target, allowing contact-induced distortion to relax while checking that the plug remains retained.
The plug is retained and contact has relaxed. Its current pitch, yaw, and lateral projection look aligned; begin a fresh straight approach from clear space.
Continue the fresh vertical approach while the tip is visibly clear; preserve the relaxed grip geometry and stop near the mouth for a contact check.
Close the remaining visible gap slowly, maintaining the present alignment and watching for the first tactile displacement at the rim.
The tip reached the mouth with stable tactile contact. Test a gentle one-millimeter insertion while keeping alignment and grip unchanged.
Tactile contact remains nearly unchanged despite tip occlusion at the socket. Continue a slow axial advance and watch for sustained slipping.
The connector slipped axially and appears slightly left of the socket center. Relieve contact while shifting one millimeter right, then reapproach gently.
Test a shallow straight insertion after lateral recentering, monitoring whether the connector advances or slips along the fingers.
Relieve the renewed axial slip and refine both pitch and yaw from the tactile edge geometry, compensating translation to preserve approximate tip centering.
Clear the tip and further correct the yaw suggested by the opposed tactile contact offsets, keeping pitch fixed and compensating lateral tip motion.
The connector is visibly clear and retained. Reapproach the mouth at the revised yaw, stopping near first contact for an alignment check.
Close the small remaining gap and test shallow insertion at the current angular alignment, watching for tactile slip rather than assuming seating.
Tactile contact remains stable at the mouth. Continue a gentle axial advance and check whether the plug advances without relative sliding.
Axial slip resumed at the rim. Lift clear and remove the small visible sideways lean, pivoting approximately about the tip while preserving depth and yaw.
Reapproach the mouth with the corrected sideways lean, keeping pitch, yaw, and depth fixed; inspect the contact before deeper insertion.
The tip is at the mouth and tactile contact is stable. Test a gentle one-millimeter insertion while monitoring plug motion relative to the fingers.
The tip is occluded at the mouth and the exposed body is shortening. Continue a controlled axial advance to test seating, monitoring whether tactile slip grows substantially.
Substantial axial contact displacement confirms obstruction rather than seating. Lift fully clear to reassess the relaxed connector orientation and position.
With the plug fully clear, correct its small visible sideways lean and residual pitch, approximately pivoting about the tip while maintaining lateral centering.
Close the visible gap with the freshly corrected orientation, keeping the grip and lateral alignment fixed; inspect at the socket mouth before deeper insertion.

notes.text: Center the held plug over the visible slot while gently correcting pitch and approaching; depth alignment remains uncertain.
Refine pitch from the opposed tactile slants, compensating translation to keep the plug tip over the slot; maintain the existing grasp.
Plug is centered in the head view. Complete the small pitch correction and descend toward the slot, with a slight depth adjustment.
The plug tip is at the socket mouth. Advance slowly along the insertion axis while preserving alignment and grasp.
Continue a small straight insertion increment; the plug remains centered and retained in the RGB views.
Apply another shallow seating increment while monitoring the contact pattern; the socket is now occluded, so insertion is not yet confirmed.
The contact shifts while the plug height stays fixed. Relieve pressure slightly and make a one-millimeter depth correction before retrying.
The plug appears constrained at the mouth. Restore the previous depth alignment and attempt a shallow, controlled seating motion.
Contact is shifting without clear insertion. Slightly tighten the grasp and lift a few millimeters to inspect and re-align rather than continue pressing.
The connector barely followed the first lift. Raise slowly with a firmer opening target to distinguish socket retention from a shallow, misaligned contact.
The plug now lifts with the fingers and the slot is visible. Make a small depth/pitch correction and re-approach slowly.
Advance to the socket mouth with submillimeter steps, keeping the corrected orientation and firm grasp.
Try a shallow straight seating motion at the newly aligned depth; monitor whether the connector follows or slides in the grasp.
The plug stops at the rim and slides upward in the fingers. Relieve the load and shift two millimeters in camera-depth toward the estimated socket center.
At the corrected depth, continue a controlled seating stroke while keeping orientation fixed; the visible housing alone does not confirm insertion depth.
Finish a shallow seating increment at fixed alignment, watching the housing and tactile slip rather than treating arm tracking as success.
The housing remains stopped as the fingers descend. Back off and shift away from the camera by three millimeters to test the unresolved socket-depth alignment.
Depth motion changed the tactile tilt, suggesting the tip is constrained. Lift farther before further alignment so the connector can clear the rim.
The plug has lifted clear in the head view. Correct the remaining pitch using the tactile slant, with translation compensation to keep the tip centered.
Orientation appears near vertical and lateral centering is good. Test a modest depth correction away from the camera while approaching above the socket.
Approach the mouth at the adjusted depth with a slow straight descent, preserving the nearly vertical orientation.
The tip has reached the slot and the tactile contact has remained stable. Attempt a shallow insertion without changing alignment.
Continue a limited seating stroke at this new depth alignment; some tactile slip is visible, so keep the descent small and reassess.
Apply one more shallow seating increment, without lateral motion, and check whether the connector settles rather than assuming the visible rim contact is insertion.
The housing is stationary while the fingers slide, so stop pressing. Lift to clear the rim and restore a less distorted grasp before another depth adjustment.
Increase clearance and move the plug three millimeters farther in depth, away from the camera, while keeping the lateral alignment fixed.
Trim the remaining pitch indicated by tactile edge slant, compensating the tip position, and lower toward the newly tested depth alignment.
Advance gently into the visible mouth at fixed pitch and depth, checking the next view for seating or renewed slip.
The unequal tactile edge heights suggest residual twist, not only depth error. Lift clear and apply a small yaw correction before another insertion attempt.
Finish the modest twist correction with the plug clear, then approach the mouth while compensating lateral tip motion.
The tip is at the visible mouth after the twist correction. Try a shallow straight insertion and inspect contact motion.
The plug again stops above the mouth and slips in the grasp. Lift off, then shift toward the camera to correct the visible depth mismatch before retrying this yaw.
Pitch and twist now appear close to socket alignment. Descend gently at the revised depth and monitor the plug rather than finger motion.
The plug is at the mouth with only slight contact shift. Continue a small straight seating stroke at this alignment.
Repeated rim contact suggests the pitch correction may have the wrong sign. Lift clear, restore the original small yaw, and test opposite pitch with tip-position compensation.
The connector is clear and centered after the opposite pitch correction. Descend to the mouth at fixed orientation for a controlled insertion test.
The corrected plug has reached the socket without obvious slip. Advance a small straight insertion increment and inspect seating.
The housing is blocked again. Lift clear and align both pitch and the smaller residual twist from the paired tactile edges, compensating translation near the plug tip.
The lifted contact pattern suggests a smaller pitch offset. Trim it while preserving the tip position and approach the centered mouth.
The plug is centered at the socket mouth. Apply a small straight insertion increment at the refined orientation.
The housing advanced to the rim. Continue a limited straight seating stroke at the current alignment, monitoring for sliding or deeper engagement.
The fingers are sliding against a stopped housing. Relieve the load and trim residual pitch, twist, and lateral centering using the paired contact edges.
Gain clear separation from the rim and test a slightly stronger pitch correction while holding the estimated plug-tip position fixed.
Approach again with the refined pitch and twist, making a small camera-depth adjustment toward the socket center.
Relieve rim contact and move two millimeters away from the camera at fixed orientation; unresolved depth alignment may be causing the repeated stop.
Test the adjusted camera-depth alignment with a slow straight seating stroke, preserving the grasp and orientation.
The housing is at the socket surface and remains retained. Continue a modest straight seating stroke rather than withdrawing immediately at rim occlusion.

notes.text: Keep the native grasp; gently center the plug over the visible slot and approach, preserving orientation while checking the tilted tactile contact.
Plug is nearly centered in the head view. Lower gradually with a small pitch correction inferred from the tactile slope, compensating the tip's lateral arc.
Maintain the centered plug and retained grasp; approach the socket vertically in small increments while watching for contact or slipping.
The tip is just above the opening. Make a small depth-centering correction while lowering slowly toward first contact; keep the grasp unchanged.
The plug now meets the slot rim. Begin a slow straight insertion, monitoring tactile retention and the plug's motion rather than assuming seating.
Continue the shallow vertical insertion with unchanged orientation and grip; contact remains visible, but full seating is not yet established.
Tactile contact shifted while the plug stayed at the rim, suggesting axial blockage. Unload slightly, then make a small depth correction before retrying.
Retry shallow vertical insertion after the depth correction; watch whether the connector follows the hand or remains blocked at the rim.
Continue a small downward insertion increment with the current alignment and unchanged grasp; monitor axial slip at the tactile contacts.
The plug remains centered and tactile contact is retained. Advance another shallow vertical increment while checking for seating or slip.

notes.text: Keep the grasp closed; begin a small pitch correction from tactile slant while lowering toward the visible socket. Depth alignment remains uncertain.
Continue modest pitch compensation about the held plug, preserving its visible lateral alignment as the gap closes.
Finish the small pitch adjustment and approach the socket lip slowly; retain the grasp and current image-center alignment.
Advance vertically in submillimeter steps to bring the plug to the slot mouth; watch for contact or deflection.
The tip meets the socket mouth without visible lateral deflection. Continue a slow insertion, maintaining pitch and grasp.
Tactile contact shifts while the plug stays at the lip, suggesting blockage. Unload upward and reduce the pitch correction while slightly adjusting depth.
Reapproach the slot at the revised pitch, with a very small lateral centering correction. Check whether the plug advances with the fingers.
Contact shifts before clear insertion. Unload the lip, then shift 1.5 mm in camera-depth to test socket alignment without forcing downward.
The plug remains at the mouth while tactile angle changes. Lift enough to clear contact and slightly close the position target to improve retention before realigning.
The plug clears the mouth and tactile contact recovers. Restore pitch compensation and move a few millimeters in depth toward the estimated socket center while still above it.
The tip is centered over the visible mouth and tactile shape remains stable. Test a slow 1.25 mm downward advance at the corrected depth.
Continue the gentle vertical insertion test. The plug remains at the mouth with little tactile change; monitor for slip rather than assuming seating.
Tactile translation suggests the tip is blocked rather than advancing. Unload slightly and add a small pitch correction, which also moves the tip toward the socket in depth.
Test insertion at the revised pitch and depth with small vertical increments, retaining the connector and monitoring tactile slip.
Tactile shift indicates blockage. Back out slightly, reduce the pitch, and move the tip back in depth before another low-force approach.
With the plug unloaded, shift 1.3 mm farther back in depth and lower gently to test the socket center at the reduced pitch.
Test a 1 mm vertical insertion at this depth alignment; watch the tactile patch for sliding or rotation rather than relying on arm tracking.
Continue by another millimeter with fixed orientation. Current contact is small; compare plug motion and tactile displacement before proceeding deeper.
The plug top moves down with the fingers while tactile shape stays nearly unchanged, consistent with entry. Maintain alignment and advance slowly.
Continue the straight insertion in 0.2 mm increments. The visible plug top continues following the gripper without substantial tactile slip.

notes.text: Adjust the held plug's pitch and yaw in small increments, approximately pivoting near its tip; preserve the current grasp and inspect alignment before descending.
Approach the socket slowly while correcting estimated fore-aft offset; retain pitch correction and grip, then reassess the visible tip-to-slot gap.
Lower another 3 mm with the plug centered over the visible slot; monitor the remaining gap and tactile contact before attempting seating.
Bring the tip to the socket mouth with a small fore-aft correction and a slow 1.75 mm descent; watch for contact or deflection.
The tip visually meets the slot mouth. Begin slow straight insertion while holding orientation and checking for tactile change or lateral deflection.
Continue the slow axial insertion; the visible lower tip is at the socket and the grasp pattern remains stable.
The tactile patches shifted during descent, suggesting the tip may be on a rim rather than seated. Unload upward 2 mm and correct fore-aft alignment slightly before retrying.
Retry a gentle 1.5 mm axial descent at the corrected fore-aft position, watching for renewed tactile displacement versus entry.
Slight tactile motion suggests rim contact. Unload, shift the tip modestly away from the camera, and finish a small pitch correction before another insertion attempt.
Test the corrected alignment with a slow 1.25 mm descent; monitor whether the plug enters or shifts upward within the grasp.
The plug remains at the surface while its tactile imprint shifts. Relieve contact and probe a 2 mm fore-aft correction toward the camera, preserving angular alignment.
Attempt a gentle insertion at the revised fore-aft alignment and compare the tactile imprint for retention versus surface blockage.
Continue only 1 mm farther at the current alignment to distinguish shallow entry from rim contact, retaining the same grasp.
The tactile contact is sliding sideways rather than staying fixed. Unload and shift 2.5 mm away from the camera to recenter the tip before probing again.
Probe straight down at the recentered position. Check the tactile patch for upward slip, which would indicate continued blockage at the socket lip.
Continue a cautious 1 mm seating motion at the current alignment; the plug overlaps the slot mouth, but entry is not yet confirmed.
The tactile contact remains near its retained-grasp pattern. Advance another 1 mm along the insertion axis while watching for displacement.

notes.text: Maintain grasp; gently reduce the apparent pitch offset and move toward the slot center while staying above it.
Complete the small pitch correction and lower gradually; plug remains retained and nearly centered over the visible slot.
Approach straight downward with fixed orientation and a tiny lateral centering correction, watching the remaining gap.
Plug appears centered at the mouth; begin a shallow insertion with small vertical increments while keeping the grasp fixed.
Contact imprint shifted while the tip barely advanced. Relieve contact slightly and correct depth alignment toward the visible slot rather than continuing to push.
The depth correction tilted the retained plug against the mouth. Undo it gently to restore a vertical plug before advancing farther.
Pitch has returned close to the retained alignment. Apply a very small depth correction and a shallow downward seating motion.
The imprint is moving relative to the fingers while the plug remains at the rim. Relieve downward pressure and test a 1 mm depth alignment correction.
Positive depth motion tilted the plug at its constrained tip. Restore the previous depth alignment and test a very shallow seating motion.
The tactile pitch is again close to vertical after compensation. Advance 1 mm downward with a small visible lateral centering correction.
The plug appears stopped at the mouth while the tactile patch slides. Lift 3 mm to clear the rim before realigning; retain a slightly smaller opening.
Increase clearance slowly and command a smaller opening to limit the observed slip before another alignment attempt.
With a visible gap restored, adjust the depth position by about 1.5 mm at the plug and refine pitch before lowering again.
Lower 1.5 mm at the revised depth alignment, retaining the plug and monitoring contact.
The plug reached the mouth without visible imprint shift. Begin another shallow downward insertion at fixed alignment.
The contact patch shifted while the tip stayed at the rim. Raise 3 mm to remove the constraint before correcting the remaining pitch error.
With clearance restored, compensate the residual tactile pitch while approximately pivoting about the connector tip.
Lower the pitch-corrected connector toward the socket without further lateral motion, checking whether contact remains stable.
The plug has reached the socket mouth with little tactile change. Try a further 1 mm straight insertion, watching for relative slip rather than assuming seating.
The imprint moved relative to the hand again. Lift off the mouth, then test a 1 mm depth correction away from the camera while preserving the pitch alignment.
Approach and test the new depth alignment in small downward steps, monitoring whether the plug moves with the hand.
The plug still stops at the rim. Clear it vertically, then test the opposite depth side of the mouth without changing pitch.
Withdraw farther to obtain unambiguous clearance, restoring the previous yaw before reassessing the retained plug's pitch and depth.
With the plug fully clear, compensate its changed tactile pitch by rotating about the approximate tip, keeping the visible lateral alignment.
Refine pitch slightly and approach the socket from clear space, stopping above the mouth for another visual check.
The retained plug is visibly centered with a small gap. Lower 3 mm at fixed pitch and depth to reach the mouth.
The approach reached the mouth without an obvious tactile shift. Test a shallow 1 mm insertion while holding the current alignment.
Repeated rim stops suggest more than depth error. Clear the socket and correct the cross-sensor skew with a modest yaw adjustment, approximately preserving the tip center.
Finish the small yaw compensation while clear, then approach cautiously without changing depth or pitch.
The plug is at the mouth with little imprint change. Test a shallow straight insertion at the revised yaw alignment.
Continue a limited 2 mm seating test with fixed alignment and retained grasp; compare plug exposure and both contact patches before making further corrections.
The latest seating test caused clear relative slip and skew. Withdraw vertically by 10 mm for definite clearance before recalibrating the plug orientation.
With definite clearance, reduce residual pitch and shift the connector tip toward the camera-side depth of the slot; retain a visible approach gap.
Approach at the new depth alignment, correcting the small visible lateral offset and preserving the now-compensated pitch.
Close the remaining visible gap while making a small residual pitch correction about the tip; keep the depth and lateral tip location approximately fixed.
The plug reached the mouth without an obvious contact-patch shift. Continue a bounded 3 mm straight seating motion at the current alignment.
The plug is stopped and the opposing imprints are strongly skewed. Clear the rim and reduce the yaw correction while keeping the tip laterally centered.
While clear, compensate the opposing-pad depth asymmetry with positive yaw about the approximate tip. The yaw sign remains uncertain, so keep the plug above the mouth.
Approach the mouth at the revised yaw without further lateral motion, monitoring whether the contact imprint remains stable.
The plug followed the approach to the mouth. Test 1.5 mm of straight insertion and inspect for renewed relative slip.
The latest test again slipped at the rim. Withdraw 5 mm, then move 4 mm away from the camera to correct the estimated plug-versus-slot depth offset, keeping orientation fixed.
Lower toward the mouth at the revised depth, leaving the orientation unchanged so the effect of this alignment correction can be assessed.
At the mouth again with a stable imprint; test one millimeter of insertion at the adjusted depth before deciding on further alignment.
Rim contact still causes slip. Withdraw well clear and undo the large yaw adjustment, approximately preserving the tip position, to reassess the opposing contact skew.
With the plug clearly free, compensate the current tactile pitch and opposing-pad depth skew together, approximately pivoting about the tip.
Keep the corrected orientation and approach with a 4 mm camera-side depth adjustment, also centering the tip over the slot in the head view.
While still clear, compensate the remaining opposing-pad depth skew with a small yaw rotation, translating to approximately preserve the tip center.
The exposed plug leans left despite the pitch/yaw correction. Correct that roll while approximately pivoting at the tip and retaining clearance.
The exposed plug now appears more vertical and centered. Approach the mouth at fixed orientation, stopping short of a deep insertion.
The plug is just at the slot with the corrected roll. Test one millimeter of straight insertion and check whether the contact patches stay fixed.
The last shallow step left the tactile patches nearly unchanged. Continue a limited 2 mm straight seating motion, preserving alignment.
The last step caused clear slip. Withdraw 8 mm, then correct the accumulated camera-side depth offset by moving 7 mm away from the camera while keeping orientation fixed.
The plug is clearly above the slot after the depth correction. Approach 6 mm straight down without adding another orientation change.
Close the small remaining gap and test a shallow insertion at the new depth while maintaining the retained plug's orientation.
The plug again stops behind the visible mouth and slips. Clear the rim, then bring its depth 5.5 mm toward the camera without changing the compensated orientation.
The plug did not clearly follow the short withdrawal. Command full closure and lift gently to establish definite clearance before another insertion attempt.
With a visible gap, compensate a little more of the opposing-pad yaw skew, approximately pivoting at the tip and maintaining clearance.
Lower through the remaining visible gap with the current yaw and grasp held fixed, stopping at the mouth.
The plug reached the mouth with little patch displacement. Continue a bounded 2 mm seating motion at fixed alignment.
The mouth still blocks advancement. Clear it vertically, then correct the estimated camera-side depth error by moving 8 mm away from the camera, with orientation fixed.
With clear space restored, reduce the residual tactile pitch error while approximately pivoting at the plug tip; approach only partway to the mouth.
Close the visible gap with a 3 mm straight approach at the corrected depth and pitch, watching for the first sign of relative slip.
The plug stops behind the visible mouth. Clear it, restore camera-side depth by about 8 mm at the tip, and make small residual pitch/yaw corrections while clear.
Approach straight down through the remaining visible gap at the corrected depth, retaining the current orientation.
The plug reached the mouth without obvious contact-patch displacement. Test a further 1.5 mm straight seating motion.
The seating test still slips. Withdraw fully and return gradually to the native holding opening so the less-distorted tactile shape can guide a fresh alignment.
While clear, correct the visible sideways lean and remaining tactile pitch, approximately pivoting about the plug tip, then approach partway toward the mouth.
Refine the small remaining lean and center the tip over the visible opening while approaching 3 mm, preserving tip depth approximately.
The tip looks vertical and centered with a small gap. Lower 2.5 mm at fixed orientation and depth to reach the mouth.
Clear the mouth and reduce the accumulated yaw by about 0.2 rad, using the opposing tactile depth offset to reassess alignment and approximately preserving the tip center.
The reduced yaw exposes a slight rightward lean. Correct that roll about the approximate tip and approach 2 mm while keeping a visible clearance.
Refine the remaining small visible lean while preserving the tip center, and lower through the last few millimeters of clearance.
At the mouth with a nearly vertical plug and stable contact shape, test one millimeter of straight insertion.
Only a small contact displacement appeared in the last step. Limit the next seating test to another millimeter, with no lateral or angular change.
The latest millimeter clearly slipped at the rim. Lift clear and make a small 1.5 mm depth correction away from the camera, keeping the improved orientation unchanged.
Close the small restored gap and test the revised depth alignment with a limited 2 mm straight downward motion.
The plug followed most of the latest approach. Test another millimeter slowly at fixed alignment, watching for renewed sliding in the fingers.
The plug remains blocked despite near-level pitch. Clear the rim and test a larger depth correction away from the camera, keeping the improved orientation unchanged.
Approach 5 mm straight down at the revised depth, stopping near the socket mouth to inspect alignment.
The plug is centered with about a millimeter of visible clearance. Close that gap slowly without changing orientation or depth.
The shallow step slipped at the rim. Clear the tip and test a 2 mm camera-side depth correction, preserving the nearly level pitch and current yaw.
Approach the mouth at the revised depth with a 2.5 mm straight downward motion, checking whether the plug continues to follow the fingers.
Continue a bounded 2.5 mm seating attempt at the current centered, nearly level alignment, watching plug exposure and contact deformation.
The contact shape shows another rim stop. Withdraw and test a 6 mm depth correction away from the camera, retaining the current near-level orientation.
Approach through the restored gap at the revised depth, preserving the nearly level plug orientation and lateral centering.
The plug stopped visibly behind the slot and slid upward in the fingers. Lift clear and return 5.5 mm toward the camera, keeping the current near-level orientation.
Close the restored gap at this intermediate depth with a 3 mm straight approach; keep orientation and grasp unchanged to assess contact.
The plug again stopped at the mouth. Try a bounded 1 mm depth and 0.5 mm lateral centering adjustment with only a shallow downward advance.
The small depth probe tilted the contact patch instead of inserting. Lift 5 mm without further rotation to read the unconstrained plug alignment.
The free contact shape is level again. Approach with a 2 mm depth correction away from the camera while keeping the visible centering and orientation fixed.
Close the remaining small gap at this depth with a limited straight descent; inspect whether the plug continues to follow the hand.
The tip remains at the rim. Test a small camera-side depth sweep with very shallow downward motion, watching for a drop into the opening rather than pushing farther.
The depth sweep tilted the plug at its constrained tip. Relieve that tilt and make a small negative yaw adjustment before another shallow seating attempt.
The contact patch has returned to a level shape. Test one millimeter of straight insertion at the slightly reduced yaw.
The plug still slides at the rim. Clear it and test a 1.5 mm lateral correction toward the visible left side of the slot, leaving pitch and depth unchanged.
The plug now appears laterally centered over the opening. Close the visible gap with a 3 mm straight approach at unchanged depth and orientation.
The plug is stopped just above the mouth. Hold height and test a 2 mm camera-side depth sweep without adding downward pressure, looking for the opening.
The depth sweep pivots the plug at a constrained tip. Clear it, restore the level-depth position, and correct the small remaining sideways lean about the approximate tip.
Approach the mouth with the plug now level and laterally centered, preserving this alignment through a 3 mm descent.
Use a small depth/lateral centering adjustment and slight yaw refinement at the mouth, limiting further downward travel to half a millimeter.
Relieve the renewed contact skew, then refine depth 1.3 mm away from the camera and slightly reduce yaw while clear of the rim.
The free imprints are level and the plug is centered. Approach 3 mm straight down at this refined depth and yaw.
Search gently across the mouth toward the camera with only 0.5 mm downward travel, checking whether the constrained tip can enter rather than simply pivot.

The sweep produced a pivot rather than entry. Clear the mouth, restore the prior depth, and remove the residual hand roll indicated by matching opposing contact endpoints, approximately preserving the tip center.
With roll removed and clear space available, compensate the small remaining tactile pitch about the approximate tip while approaching partway to the mouth.
Approach through the visible gap with fixed pitch and yaw, making a small leftward centering correction toward the slot.
Relieve the rim contact briefly, correct the remaining visible rightward offset by 1 mm, and return slowly to the same approach height.
The tip is now laterally centered. Refine yaw by a small amount inferred from the opposing contact offset while testing less than a millimeter of insertion.
The plug still slips at the mouth. Clear the rim and sample a nearby depth 1.5 mm farther from the camera while retaining the current centered orientation.
Approach the visible gap slowly at the new depth, preserving the plug's centered orientation and grasp.
The plug followed the last descent with stable contact patches. Close the remaining millimeter slowly at fixed alignment.
The tip is still blocked despite good centering. Relieve contact briefly and make small pitch/yaw corrections inferred from the free tactile shape, approximately pivoting at the tip.
Test one millimeter of straight insertion after the small angular refinement; keep the grasp and lateral position fixed.
The plug is still stopped visibly behind the opening. Withdraw clearly, then bring it 8 mm toward the camera without changing the nearly level orientation.
Approach through the restored gap at the camera-side depth, with a small visible lateral centering correction and fixed orientation.
The plug followed the approach with stable contact patches. Close the remaining visible gap with a slow 2 mm straight descent.
The plug reached the mouth with no obvious patch displacement. Test one millimeter of straight insertion while retaining the current alignment.
The last millimeter slipped at the mouth. Relieve contact and correct the small residual pitch by 0.01 rad about the approximate tip, retaining depth and lateral alignment.
Lower through the restored small gap at the refined pitch, keeping the tip depth and lateral location fixed.
The plug followed the latest approach to the mouth with little contact movement. Test another millimeter of straight insertion at unchanged alignment.

Maintain alignment and the retained grasp while advancing another millimeter into the socket; monitor the plug relative to the fixed block.

notes.text: Keep the native grasp; make a small downward approach and center the plug over the visible slot. Depth and in-grasp tilt remain uncertain.
Continue the short approach, with a very small tilt correction to center the lower end while preserving the grasp.
The plug appears centered above the slot. Approach vertically in small steps, maintaining the current orientation.

Continue the sideways inspection turn while keeping the grasp center above the block. The plug remains occluded, so do not descend or assume retention.
The side view reveals a dark connector near the pads. Make another small grasp-centered pitch correction toward tip-down, keeping the connector above the socket and checking its visible end.
Turn farther sideways around the held connector to expose its tip. Maintain height and the closed grasp; orientation and retention need visual confirmation before another approach.

The connector is still largely hidden. Reduce the pitch while maintaining the sideways view and approximate grasp center, so its exposed end can be inspected instead of continuing an unverified rotation.
Return gradually toward an upright, front-visible grasp while keeping the connector center above the block. Do not descend while its actual orientation remains occluded.
Complete the return to a near-vertical hand while holding the grasp center clear of the socket. This should expose whether the connector is upright or still sideways between the pads.
The connector is visible between the pads again. Remove the remaining yaw and move partway toward the socket, staying well above it to inspect the exposed tip.
Bring the visible connector over the slit and lower while retaining about a centimeter of clearance. Its exposed end is short, so reassess before contact rather than drive the fingers into the block.
Lower the retained connector another 8 mm toward the centered slit, leaving a small visible gap. Keep orientation fixed and inspect the short exposed tip before touching the block.
The exposed connector is much narrower than the socket, suggesting a yaw mismatch after recovery. Lift clear and begin turning about vertical to bring its broad face into alignment.

notes.text: Begin gently straightening the held plug, translating to roughly preserve its tip position and retaining the existing grasp.
Continue small rotational alignment above the slot; keep the plug centered while reducing the visible gap slowly.
Finish straightening in small increments with tip-pivot compensation; nudge the plug toward the socket center while still above it.
The plug appears laterally centered and nearly vertical. Lower it a few millimeters while maintaining orientation and the existing grasp.
Approach the socket entrance slowly with the plug centered; preserve the grasp and watch for contact or misalignment.
The plug tip is at the socket entrance. Advance gently downward while keeping the current alignment and grasp.
Continue a slow, straight insertion; the tip appears centered at the slot, but seating is not yet confirmed.
Advance another millimeter slowly along the slot axis, preserving alignment and grasp; seating remains visually uncertain.
Continue a small axial seating motion while retaining the grasp; the connector is at the socket, but full insertion is not yet clear.
Make another small straight seating motion, keeping the plug aligned and the grasp unchanged; full insertion remains uncertain.
Use a smaller final axial advance while watching the connector at the socket; keep the existing grasp and orientation.
Make a very small seating advance, then pause with the grasp unchanged. The socket interface is partly occluded, so seating is not confirmed.
Hold the current alignment briefly to let the connector settle; the occluded interface does not yet establish full seating.
Try a further half-millimeter axial seating motion without changing the grasp; the tip remains centered visually but the interface is occluded.
Use a very small axial advance, then settle; the plug meets the slot visually, but the occluded contact does not confirm seating.
Try a submillimeter depth-alignment correction with minimal downward motion; the plug is centered laterally, but its seating remains occluded.
Refine alignment along the camera-depth direction without further downward pressure; compare the plug with the fixed slot after this small correction.
Lift five millimeters to inspect the plug/socket relationship; the visible plug base has stopped descending, so avoid continuing to press without checking alignment.
The plug lifted with the hand and remains above the slot. Re-approach gently with a small depth correction, retaining lateral alignment.
Back off slightly and correct the camera-depth alignment toward the slot center before another insertion attempt; keep the connector grasped.
Re-approach the visible slot at the corrected depth with small axial steps, preserving the retained connector and watching the entrance.
Lower gently at the corrected alignment. The connector remains over the slot; watch whether the body seats as the fingers approach the socket surface.
Continue a gentle axial insertion at the current centered alignment, monitoring the connector body rather than assuming seating from hand motion.
Try one millimeter of controlled axial seating at the corrected alignment. The socket masks the tip, so inspect the connector's motion before further adjustment.
The connector base appears stationary despite descent. Lift to clear the entrance and reassess depth and angular alignment rather than pressing further.
Clear the lip slightly and shift the plug tip about two millimeters away from the camera, with a small pitch correction before re-approaching.
Approach at the newly adjusted depth and pitch, stopping short of the visible socket lip to check alignment before seating.
Lower the retained plug toward the entrance at the revised alignment, using a short descent to check whether its base follows the hand.
Close the small visible gap at the revised alignment with a 1.25 mm descent, watching whether the connector follows rather than assuming insertion.
Make a submillimeter depth correction and gentle seating advance; the housing is close to the socket surface, so avoid a large push.
Clear the socket lip and shift slightly toward the camera to test depth alignment; repeated downward motion has not visibly seated the plug.
Adjust the plug's pitch slightly with tip-pivot compensation and move its tip toward the camera about 1.5 mm, then approach the socket gently.
Refine depth alignment slightly away from the camera while making a short, gentle axial insertion at the corrected pitch.
Apply only a small final axial advance, then hold. The connector body is at the socket surface; further seating is visually uncertain.
Back off the lip slightly and adjust depth and pitch by a small amount. The plug remains retained, but its stationary base does not establish insertion.
Re-approach with a small depth and lateral correction at the current pitch, using a gentle 1.5 mm descent and preserving the grasp.
Center the plug a fraction of a millimeter left over the visible slot and make a short seating advance, then pause to inspect.
Refine lateral registration with the slot by 0.3 mm and hold without further descent; the connector base is already at the socket surface.
Lift clear of the socket to expose its entrance and the plug tip; repeated contact-level adjustments have not established correct angular alignment.
Use the newly exposed slot to center the plug slightly right, with a small depth correction and a short descent that leaves clearance for inspection.
Approach the exposed slot straight down while slightly reducing the opening target; the plug appears to have shifted upward between the fingers during prior contacts.
Advance the centered plug 1.5 mm along the insertion axis with the adjusted opening, watching whether the body seats or shifts relative to the fingers.
Slightly reduce the opening target and make a one-millimeter seating advance, monitoring the plug relative to the fingers rather than inferring insertion from hand tracking.
Maintain the visibly centered plug and adjusted grasp for a short axial seating advance, then pause; the socket hides the tip, so seating remains uncertain.
Lift the retained connector clear of the lip to inspect its actual tilt and tip alignment; further descent at the same pose has not visibly advanced the body.
Correct the visible cross-slot tilt slightly while above the entrance, compensating laterally to keep the plug tip near the slot center.
Test a modest pitch correction while clear of the socket, compensating hand translation to keep the retained plug tip near the visible entrance.
Approach the exposed entrance at the revised pitch, keeping the plug centered and retained; stop near the lip to assess its motion.
Bring the revised alignment gently to the socket mouth, then pause to inspect whether the connector follows the hand into the opening.
Advance one millimeter along the nearly vertical plug axis, then hold at the socket. Inspect seating before making any further alignment changes.
The plug body is resting at the socket mouth. Keep the hand stationary and gently loosen the fingers to inspect whether the socket supports the connector without further downward sliding.
The released plug remains at the socket but looks tilted. Lift the open fingers slightly to expose its orientation and support before attempting a corrective grasp.
Lower the open fingers around the exposed connector, centering slightly left on its tilted body for a controlled corrective grasp.
Center on the exposed upright connector and close the fingers gradually for a fresh grasp, without pushing it farther into the socket.
The closing fingers visibly tipped the connector instead of securing it squarely. Open and lift slightly to expose its resting orientation before correcting the grasp.
Approach the fallen connector with open fingers, centering slightly right and lowering toward its sides without closing yet.
Position the open pads around the fallen connector's sides, shifting slightly toward the camera and lowering only three millimeters before closing.
Lower the pads slightly alongside the fallen connector and close gradually for a recovery grasp; verify retention visually before lifting far.
Finish closing around the fallen connector and make a short test lift to check whether it is retained between the pads.
The fallen connector did not follow the test lift. Open and move the pads toward its nearer black housing before attempting a lower recovery grasp.

notes.text: Bring the retained plug toward the slot center and reduce its apparent tilt with a small compensated rotation; descend cautiously.
Maintain the visible lateral centering, reduce forward tilt with translation compensation, and approach the slot slowly.
Continue squaring the connector over the fixed slot, compensating the hand rotation to keep the tip centered; preserve clearance during alignment.
Square the plug axis while compensating tip motion and approach the visible socket opening; retain the existing grip.
The plug is centered over the visible opening and nearly touching it. Begin a short, straight insertion while keeping the grasp and orientation fixed.
Continue a shallow straight insertion with the plug visually centered, retaining the grip and monitoring its contact with the slot.
Advance another shallow increment into the slot with the current visual centering and orientation; keep the connector grasped.
Continue a short, slow insertion while preserving the visible centering. The plug-slot contact is partly occluded, so limit further travel and reassess.
Maintain alignment and advance only 0.75 mm. The connector remains over the opening, but seating is visually ambiguous; preserve the grip and reassess.
Make a final shallow downward increment without lateral motion; the plug covers the opening, but seating is still occluded.
Pause at the current insertion depth and retain the connector. The opening is occluded, so assess stability before applying further downward travel.
The plug remains centered and retained. Advance one millimeter in small increments to test further seating without changing lateral alignment.
Continue a limited straight seating motion, keeping the plug centered and grasp unchanged. The socket occludes the tip, so completion remains uncertain.
The plug base has stopped moving visibly despite hand descent. Ease upward slightly while retaining the grasp to avoid pushing against a potentially misaligned rim.
Hold steady after relieving downward travel. The connector remains at the socket mouth; its hidden tip makes seating uncertain, so avoid further forceful motion.
Withdraw a few millimeters while keeping the grasp to expose the plug-slot relationship; the stationary plug base during descent leaves alignment uncertain.
The lifted plug remains retained and laterally centered. Make a small depth-axis correction away from the camera while approaching, since the earlier contact may have been on the socket rim.
Approach the socket at the corrected depth-axis position with a short straight descent; the plug remains retained with a small visible gap above the opening.
Close the remaining visible gap at the adjusted position using a shallow descent, keeping the connector centered and retained.
Advance a shallow insertion at the corrected depth-axis position. The plug covers the slot mouth; maintain the grip and assess the visible body rather than assuming tracking proves seating.
Try another limited straight insertion at the adjusted alignment. Monitor movement of the visible plug body; the tip is hidden by the socket rim.
The visible plug has not followed the recent descent convincingly. Retract vertically to expose the mouth and relieve possible rim contact before revising alignment.
With the tip now clear of the mouth, shift it two millimeters farther from the camera and approach gently; lateral centering appears close.
Approach the visible opening at the revised depth position in a two-millimeter descent, holding orientation and grip fixed to compare tip motion with hand motion.
The tip is immediately above the slot at the revised depth alignment. Descend 1.5 mm with the grasp and orientation unchanged, checking for entry rather than relying on hand tracking.
Apply a submillimeter centering correction and shallow seating motion at the revised depth alignment. Keep the plug grasped; its tip remains occluded by the socket.
The connector body has stopped following hand descent. Slightly reduce the opening target and lift clear to check retention before correcting angular alignment.
The lifted connector follows the hand and is centered laterally. Approach the opening again with the slightly smaller grip target, leaving angular and depth-axis alignment unchanged to check entry.
Close the small visible gap with a controlled 1.5 mm descent at the current alignment and tighter grasp, then inspect whether the connector follows into the opening.
Lift clear of possible rim contact and make a small pitch correction, compensating hand translation to keep the plug tip near the opening's depth position.
The lifted plug is retained with a visible gap above the slot. Approach at the corrected pitch with a short vertical descent, preserving lateral centering.
Try a shallow seating increment at the corrected pitch. Watch the upper connector body as the tip becomes occluded, maintaining the tighter grip.
The visible tip again stops above the opening. Lift clear and test a small depth correction toward the camera, opposite the earlier unsuccessful depth adjustments, while retaining the current pitch.
Approach at the revised depth and pitch, adding a submillimeter leftward correction to center the visible tip over the slot. Keep the connector grasped.
Lift slightly and shift two millimeters toward the camera to test the remaining depth-axis alignment; lateral centering looks close, but entry is not confirmed.
Lower through the visible gap at the latest depth correction, keeping pitch and lateral centering fixed. Check whether the connector enters or stops on the rim.
Try a shallow seating increment at the latest depth alignment. Keep the retained plug centered and monitor for entry; the tip is hidden by the socket.
Entry remains unconfirmed after depth adjustments. Withdraw and test the opposite pitch correction, compensating translation approximately to preserve tip alignment while clear of the rim.
Approach the visible slot with the revised pitch and a one-millimeter depth correction, keeping the retained plug laterally centered.
Close the visible gap at the revised pitch with a two-millimeter straight descent. Compare connector-body motion against the fixed slot before making any further alignment change.
The connector rests at the socket mouth after several shallow approaches. Relax the fingers without moving the hand to check whether it remains supported in the slot.
The released connector remains upright at the opening. Raise the open hand slightly to inspect whether it stays supported without finger contact.
The connector stands at the mouth but full seating is unconfirmed. Regrasp its upper body and lift slightly to expose the slot and reassess alignment.
The connector tipped and is not retained. Open the fingers and lower around its body for recovery rather than continuing insertion with an empty grasp.
The tipped connector lies between the open fingertips. Center slightly on its body and close progressively at the current height to recover retention without pressing onto the block.
Lift the recently closed grasp five millimeters to check whether the diagonal connector is retained before attempting to straighten it.
The diagonal connector followed the lift. Raise it clear while beginning a small roll to straighten its visible axis, compensating hand translation around the grasp region.
The connector is no longer retained after the roll. Open the fingers, return the hand upright, and lower around the tipped body for a deeper recovery grasp.
The connector lies flat, forward and slightly right of the fingers. Recenter the open grasp toward its body with a little vertical clearance before closing.
Lower the open fingers around the flat connector for deeper pad overlap, then close progressively. Retention must be checked with a small lift.
Lift the closed grasp ten millimeters to verify recovery of the flat connector and expose its orientation before attempting to straighten it.
The recovered connector is hanging at an angle near the fingertip edges. Close fully and lift slowly for clearance, checking retention before rotating.
The connector follows the closed grasp but lies across the fingers. Lift for clearance and begin a small pitch rotation about the grasp region to turn its end downward; monitor retention.
The connector remains at the closed fingertips with its free end diagonally down-right. Begin turning that end downward while compensating hand position to preserve clearance and inspect retention.
The recovered connector follows the grasp and points down-right. Rotate it further toward vertical above the socket, compensating translation to keep the grasp region clear of the block.
Continue rotating the recovered connector toward vertical while keeping its grasp region above the block; verify that it follows the fingers rather than slipping.
The retained plug is still leaning slightly right. Continue straightening it above the opening with a compensated roll, keeping the grasp region clear of the block.
The connector has separated from the fingers and rests on the block. Open and return the hand toward upright with upward clearance before attempting another grasp.
Return the open hand upright above the loose connector, moving the grasp center slightly left and away from the camera. Keep clearance while recovering alignment.
Lower the open, upright fingers around the flat connector, which is now centered in the gap. Keep lateral position fixed and inspect pad overlap before closing.

notes.text: Keep the grasp; cautiously reduce visible pitch offset and bring the plug toward the socket center while closing part of the vertical gap.
Plug is retained and nearly centered over the visible slot. Finish the small pitch correction and descend slowly, keeping clearance for final alignment.
The plug is almost vertically aligned with the slot. Lower by 2.5 mm with a very small lateral centering adjustment, retaining the current grasp and orientation.
The connector now reaches the mouth of the socket. Continue a short, straight downward insertion while preserving lateral alignment and grip.
Advance another 1.5 mm along the insertion direction. The socket remains fixed and the plug appears centered; monitor seating rather than interpreting tracking as success.
Continue a slow seating motion with only a 0.2 mm depth-axis centering correction; retain grip and check whether the visible body continues entering the slot.
Seating is visually uncertain: the plug body may have stopped moving with the fingers. Relieve contact by 1 mm and make a small pitch correction about the tip before another insertion attempt.
Apply a final small pitch adjustment while keeping the tip nearly stationary laterally, then cautiously re-advance 1.5 mm into the socket.
The plug appears flush with the slot. Use only a tiny final seating increment and hold the grasp to allow the contact to settle; completion is not yet confirmed.
Seating remains uncertain. Remove a small cross-axis tilt about the plug tip and slightly reduce commanded opening to limit visible slipping, with only 0.25 mm of descent.
Lift 2.5 mm to relieve the uncertain contact and verify that the plug follows the grasp before making a finer socket-depth alignment correction.
The plug did not visibly follow the small lift. Close the gripper further and retract only 3 mm to distinguish a slipping grasp from a connector caught at the socket mouth.
With the narrower grasp, retract 5 mm slowly to clear the socket lip and check whether the connector is retained before re-aligning.
The plug now visibly follows the lift and is centered above the opening. Re-approach the socket mouth with the established narrower grasp, preserving alignment.
The plug edge appears skewed relative to the slot. Back off 2 mm and make a modest yaw correction about the connector, checking the edge alignment before insertion.
Maintain clearance and continue the small yaw correction. Compare the exposed lower connector edge with the socket's long edge before re-approaching.
A residual slant remains on the exposed plug edge. Correct a small roll component about the tip while maintaining clearance and the closed grasp.
The lower plug edge now looks closer to parallel with the socket. Center it slightly left and descend 3 mm to approach the mouth, keeping orientation fixed.
The connector has reached the visible socket mouth. Attempt a slow 2 mm insertion with the corrected orientation and closed grasp, checking that the body moves rather than slips.
The exposed body appears slightly lower but seating remains uncertain. Continue only 1.5 mm straight down, retaining the current alignment and grip.
The fingers are approaching the block while the plug body stops descending. Leave the plug supported at the mouth, open slightly and raise the hand 6 mm to regrasp higher on the housing.
With the plug supported and clearly visible, level the open fingers and center them on its upper housing for a higher, unobstructed regrasp.
Close around the upper housing, then lift 2 mm to establish retention and clear the lip before correcting the plug's visible sideways lean.
Lift a further 4 mm with the closed regrasp. Check that the housing clears the socket lip before changing its alignment.
The lifted housing is visibly skewed. Correct part of its yaw and sideways lean while keeping the lower end near the socket center and maintaining clearance.
The correction improved the exposed edge. Reduce the remaining skew in smaller increments, keeping the tip above the slot and nearly stationary.
The exposed plug edge now looks nearly parallel to the slot. Approach by 3 mm with a small lateral centering correction, maintaining the higher grasp.
The plug has reached the socket mouth with clearance below the fingers. Attempt a slow 2 mm insertion without changing its corrected orientation.
The body may be catching at the lip. Make a small socket-depth alignment adjustment with slight initial relief, then probe downward gently; retain the centered lateral alignment.
Test the adjusted depth alignment with a short 1.75 mm straight insertion, watching for motion of the connector housing rather than finger motion alone.
The housing has stopped descending. Probe the poorly observed socket-depth direction by 3 mm with minimal downward travel, keeping the visible lateral alignment unchanged.
Depth translation alone did not visibly seat the housing. Relieve contact and test a small pitch correction about the lower end, preserving its approximate socket position.
Probe a few millimeters toward the camera while lowering slowly. The lower edge is visually parallel to the slot, but its depth alignment is still ambiguous.
Make a smaller reverse depth correction while lightly advancing downward. Keep the visible connector edge parallel and avoid a large seating push.
Refine the residual pitch and yaw with a tip-preserving motion, then gently re-enter. The lower edge is centered but full insertion is still not visible.
Shift the lower end slightly left to match the visible slot center and probe 1 mm toward the camera while gently lowering. Keep the corrected orientation fixed.
The housing is still stopped at the mouth. Lift 9 mm to remove contact and expose the lower connector for a fresh alignment check, keeping the grasp closed.
The newly exposed lower blade looks narrow/skewed. Raise it clear and test a small yaw change so its projected width and edge direction can be compared with the socket.
The exposed blade widened with the last yaw change. Continue that rotation above the socket while approximately holding its tip position; do not descend until the blade faces the opening.
Continue yaw alignment with the connector lifted. Its exposed broad face is becoming more visible; preserve clearance and check the lower edge against the slot.
The last yaw sweep obscured the blade and did not establish alignment. Return toward a broad face parallel to the slot while keeping the connector safely above it.
Complete the return toward the earlier parallel-edge orientation and descend only part of the visible gap. Keep the blade above the mouth for the next alignment check.
The exposed lower blade is narrower than the slot. Lift clear and rotate toward the direction that previously widened it, keeping its lower end approximately centered.
Continue the yaw search above the opening and recenter slightly left. Use the exposed lower blade, not the partly occluded upper housing, to judge alignment.
Correct the unintended pitch component from the preceding rotation while keeping the connector lifted; reassess the exposed blade before further alignment.
Keep the connector clear of the block and continue the yaw sweep to expose the full lower blade; compensate lateral motion approximately and reassess before descending.
The visible lower edge is broad and nearly parallel to the slot. Center it leftward and close only part of the vertical gap while holding this orientation.
The lower edge is centered with a small remaining gap. Approach the socket mouth by 3 mm, keeping the established yaw and closed grasp.
The connector has reached the socket mouth. Advance 2 mm slowly with fixed alignment; the housing is partly occluded, so seating remains uncertain.
Probe a further 1.5 mm downward without changing orientation. The fingers obscure the connector, so this is a limited seating attempt, not a completion claim.
Insertion is obscured and unconfirmed. Lift clear of the block and return toward a view that exposes the connector, keeping the grasp closed.
Keep the plug clear and undo the large yaw excursion to expose its face again. Re-establish visual alignment before any further insertion.
Keep clearance above the socket and turn the exposed connector closer to a face-on view, compensating approximately for tip motion. Recheck its lower edge before descending.
The lower blade is clearly too narrow in this view. Turn toward its broad face while maintaining clearance and approximately stabilizing the exposed tip over the socket.
The exposed blade widens with this yaw direction but is right of the socket. Continue the turn while recentering left and correcting the uncertain camera-depth offset, staying well above the opening.
The exposed lower edge is now broad and centered. Close most of the vertical gap while shifting slightly away from the camera, leaving a small clearance for the final approach.
Close the remaining small gap to the socket mouth without changing the broad-edge alignment. Check contact and finger clearance before attempting further insertion.
The connector is supported at the socket, but the fingers have little insertion clearance. Open and raise the hand 8 mm to regrasp higher on the housing.
With the connector supported, center the open hand over its upper housing and turn the fingers toward a face-on regrasp. Maintain the higher grasp height.
Finish leveling the open hand while the plug remains supported. The upper housing is now visible for a centered regrasp.

Complete the small inclination correction while easing the tube 1 mm forward and centering the remaining asymmetric rim.
Rim is now laterally centered. Maintain the corrected inclination and make a slow 4.5 mm axial insertion.
The exposed rim narrows evenly as the tube advances. Continue another 5 mm along the held axis without releasing.
The tube now covers the entrance evenly. Continue a controlled 6 mm axial advance and monitor retention and seating.
Maintain the aligned shaft and closed grasp while advancing another 6 mm into the inclined slot.
The shaft remains at the entrance with no visible lateral rim. Continue slow axial insertion, preserving the current alignment.
Continue another 6 mm along the tube axis; the visible shaft is shortening while remaining aligned with the slot.

The left rim remains visible. Reverse the tiny lateral probe to center the tube while advancing only a few millimeters.
The rim is nearly centered around the tube. Preserve orientation and grasp for another short axial insertion, watching for shortening of the exposed tube.
The entrance rim has become occluded and the tube remains held. Advance gently along the same axis without changing the lateral alignment.

The lateral probe moved the hole toward the tube. Continue that correction and finish matching the incline while only gently approaching.
The tube and hole are now laterally centered. Advance about 4.5 mm along the inclined axis with a very small final tilt correction.
The rim is nearly concentric with the tube. Continue a slow axial insertion while keeping the grasp and orientation fixed.
